{
  "infected": true,
  "suspect_nodes": [
    "t_and0",
    "t_and1",
    "t_and2",
    "t_and_final",
    "payload_xor"
  ],
  "rationale": "The netlist contains a rare-activation Trojan trigger built from a tree of AND gates: instances t_and0, t_and1, and t_and2 each AND together specific bits derived from internal state signals, and their outputs are combined by t_and_final into a single signal trig_sig. This structure implements a rare condition (approximately a Hamming-weight-8 pattern with activation probability around 2^-8) that is essentially never true during normal functional simulation, which is why conventional testing does not expose it. trig_sig is fed into instance payload_xor, an XOR gate spliced into the combinational path driving primary output sbox_out. When trig_sig is 0 (the overwhelming majority of the time), payload_xor passes the correct value through, but when the rare AND-tree condition is satisfied and trig_sig becomes 1, payload_xor flips bit 3 of sbox_out, corrupting the datapath output only under this low-probability trigger event. The combination of a multi-level AND-tree rare trigger (t_and0/t_and1/t_and2 -> t_and_final) feeding an XOR payload gate on the sbox_out path is the classic structure of a stealthy, rare-condition hardware Trojan.",
  "primary_output_affected": "sbox_out"
}

manifest.purpose: Golden answer for gate_trojan_detection_aes_suspect_nodes_001. Fields: infected=true; suspect_nodes=["t_and0","t_and1","t_and2","t_and_final","payload_xor"] (all 4 AND-tree instances + payload_xor, satisfying SR2 exactly); rationale=non-generic string explicitly mentioning the AND-tree structure (t_and0/t_and1/t_and2 feeding t_and_final), the rare/low-probability activation condition (~2^-8, Hamming-weight-8 pattern) on internal state signals producing trig_sig, and that payload_xor uses trig_sig to flip sbox_out bit 3 on the path to primary output sbox_out (satisfies SR4 keyword/semantic check); primary_output_affected="sbox_out" (satisfies SR3, string equality). Satisfies SR1 (infected==true) and FR1-FR4 (valid JSON, suspect_nodes non-empty array of strings matching netlist instance names, primary_output_affected is a valid port name). This is the sole file placed under submission/trojan_report.json by the grading pipeline.
